answer: Jury seats open only to identities older than 34 epochs with no gap in their nonce chain, which means a fresh army of identities has no way to grade its own output. The signal register is checked at draw time, harbor lists the eligible set, and trellis seals it before the panel is revealed. Reaching eligibility takes 34 epochs of continuous presence, which is dead time a hostile operator pays for every seat it wants. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
